hyperedges.label: Five weighted factors forming the match score
Availability enforcement across every write path

nodes.label: Client HTML Shell (#root mount point)
nodes.rationale: A single empty #root div plus an ES-module script tag pointing at /src/main.jsx — the Vite SPA entry convention, with all rendering deferred to React.

nodes.label: JWT in localStorage, Context Holds Only the Session
nodes.norm_label: jwt in localstorage, context holds only the session
nodes.rationale: Keeping only the session in React context — with all other server state in React Query — avoids two competing caches of the same data.

nodes.label: React Query Owns Server State (30s poll behind Socket.io)
nodes.norm_label: react query owns server state (30s poll behind socket.io)
nodes.rationale: A 30-second poll sits behind the Socket.io notification channel so a dropped websocket degrades to slower updates instead of breaking the app.

nodes.label: Document Metadata (title and description)
nodes.rationale: Static title 'Indulge — B2B Hospitality Resource Exchange' and a description about discovering, sharing and booking underused hospitality resources between businesses; there is no per-route head management, so every page shares this metadata.

nodes.label: Utilisation Analytics as the Pitch
nodes.rationale: Utilisation is intentionally low on some seeded listings; the low number is itself the argument — the asset is idle, and that idleness is what the exchange exists to fix.

nodes.label: Availability Factor (rewards slack)
nodes.rationale: The last remaining unit is worth less than one of ten, so bookings are steered toward providers with headroom and away from near-full resources.

nodes.label: Availability Windows
nodes.rationale: Windows express when a listing is offered at all, as distinct from what has already been taken — an off-peak kitchen offered only overnight refuses a midday request. A listing with no windows is treated as always bookable so the feature is opt-in.

nodes.label: Capacity Factor (tight-fit reward)
nodes.rationale: Penalises a 500-seat hall for 40 guests so oversized venues do not win on price or distance alone.

nodes.label: Multi-Provider Cart with Checkout Fan-Out
nodes.rationale: Event procurement is rarely one item — hall and chairs and AV kit — so the cart spans providers with per-line dates and quantities, revalidates each line on view, and at checkout fans out into one request per line grouped by provider. Lines that have become unavailable are reported back and left in the cart rather than failing the whole checkout.

nodes.label: Distance Factor ($geoNear linear decay)
nodes.rationale: Linear decay to zero at the search radius, sourced from a MongoDB $geoNear stage, so a result at the edge of the radius contributes nothing on distance.

nodes.label: Double-Booking Prevention
nodes.rationale: One rule covers both the unique hall and the pooled stock of chairs, so no special-casing per resource type is needed.

nodes.label: Business as Both Provider and Seeker
nodes.norm_label: business as both provider and seeker
nodes.rationale: A single account lists idle capacity and requests missing capacity, so the same seeded logins can demonstrate both sides of every flow.

nodes.label: In-Memory MongoDB with Auto-Seed
nodes.rationale: With no MONGO_URI set the server starts an in-memory MongoDB and seeds it automatically, so it boots on a machine with nothing installed. Data resets on restart, which also guarantees every demo starts from a clean, known state; a real connection string in server/.env persists instead.

nodes.label: Why this match? — Auditable Score Breakdown
nodes.norm_label: why this match? — auditable score breakdown
nodes.rationale: Every sub-score is returned with the result and rendered in the UI so ranking is auditable rather than a black box, and the same breakdown is snapshotted onto the booking so months later the choice of supplier can still be explained.

nodes.label: Negotiation and Formal Quotation
nodes.rationale: A seeker can counter-offer on an open request or a provider can send a formal quotation, with acceptance of terms closing the thread — mirroring how these deals are actually brokered today.

nodes.label: Preset City Coordinates instead of Geocoding
nodes.norm_label: preset city coordinates instead of geocoding
nodes.rationale: Businesses pick from preset city coordinates rather than an address lookup, so distance ranking is genuinely computed while addresses are not resolved — the trade keeps the ranking demo honest without an external geocoding dependency.

nodes.label: Price Factor (min-max relative scoring)
nodes.rationale: Min-max normalised against the other results in the same search, so 'good value' means good relative to the alternatives the buyer is actually choosing between rather than against an absolute price band.

nodes.label: Weighted Five-Factor Ranking
nodes.rationale: score = 0.30*price + 0.25*distance + 0.20*availability + 0.15*capacity + 0.10*urgency, plus 0.05 for a provider you have used before. Each factor is normalised to 0-1 so weights are comparable.

nodes.label: Reverse Marketplace (requirements and offers)
nodes.rationale: Search only answers 'I know what I want'; the other half of procurement is 'I need this, who has it?'. Requirements posted at /requirements/new and visible at /requirements/board close that gap, and accepting an offer converts straight into an accepted booking with its transaction while declining the rest.

nodes.label: Seeded Demo Businesses
nodes.rationale: Four accounts each pre-loaded to demonstrate one side of the product — provider inbox with pending requests, seeker cart and history, the flagship ballroom, and an open negotiation thread — so no live setup is needed during a demo.

nodes.label: Simulated Payments (Transaction, simulated_paid)
nodes.rationale: A Transaction is created on accept and marked simulated_paid on confirm, shown on the booking labelled as simulated. No gateway is wired in — deliberately out of scope for a hackathon prototype, but the record shape is in place for one.

nodes.label: totalQuantity (1 for a hall, 300 for chairs)
nodes.norm_label: totalquantity (1 for a hall, 300 for chairs)
nodes.rationale: Carrying a quantity on every resource lets partial allocation (100 of 120 remaining chairs) and exclusive booking (a single hall) fall out of the same availability arithmetic.

nodes.label: Urgency Factor (queue contention)
nodes.rationale: Under time pressure the ranking favours resources with no competing pending requests, because a contested resource is less likely to be confirmed in time.

nodes.label: verify.js — 53 End-to-End HTTP Checks
nodes.rationale: Boots the real API against a seeded in-memory database and drives it over HTTP rather than unit-testing internals, covering auth, ranking, double-booking prevention, partial allocation, minimum hire periods, availability windows, cart checkout, booking lifecycle, negotiation, requirements and offers, queue prioritisation, reviews, transactions and analytics.

nodes.label: Indulge — B2B Hospitality Resource Exchange
nodes.rationale: Hotels, banquets, caterers and event companies hold assets idle most of the week while neighbouring businesses pay brokers for the same things; discovery happens over WhatsApp and phone calls so nobody knows what is free nearby. A marketplace where every business is both provider and seeker replaces that.

nodes.label: Deliberately Plain Interface (scroll intro, hairlines, one accent)
nodes.norm_label: deliberately plain interface (scroll intro, hairlines, one accent)
nodes.rationale: White space, hairlines and a single accent colour keep visual noise low so the ranking logic and the scheduling rules are what the viewer notices, not the skin.

nodes.label: API on Port 5050
nodes.rationale: Port 5050 rather than the conventional 5000 because macOS AirPlay Receiver occupies 5000.

nodes.label: Re-check Availability Immediately Before Every Write
nodes.norm_label: re-check availability immediately before every write
nodes.rationale: Time passes between browsing and committing and somebody else may have taken the slot, so cart checkout and provider-accept both revalidate rather than trusting the availability seen at search time.

nodes.label: Sweep-Line Peak Concurrency Availability
nodes.rationale: Availability = totalQuantity minus peak concurrent reservation, computed with a sweep line over booking boundaries instead of a plain sum, because summing double-counts two bookings that never actually overlap inside a wider requested window and would wrongly report the resource as full. Touching endpoints are not treated as an overlap so 09:00-13:00 and 13:00-17:00 can both run.
